quantitiesAndSymbols.K: Inertial frame in which the rod initially moves.
quantitiesAndSymbols.K_1: Inertial rest frame of the rod, moving at speed v relative to K.
quantitiesAndSymbols.v: Relative speed; the contraction inequality applies for 0 < v < c.
quantitiesAndSymbols.c: Light speed, the same in all inertial frames.
quantitiesAndSymbols.l_0: Proper length, measured in the rod's rest frame.
quantitiesAndSymbols.l: Longitudinal length measured from endpoint positions recorded simultaneously in K.
quantitiesAndSymbols.tau_0: Round-trip proper time on the clock at rest with endpoint A in K_1.
quantitiesAndSymbols.tau: Elapsed coordinate time in K between emission at A and reception at the moving A.
quantitiesAndSymbols.AB,A_1B_1,A_2B_2: Rod positions in K at emission, reflection, and reception.

items.meaning: Lesson 97: relativity of distance.
One rod is at rest in K_1, which moves relative to K at v; its proper length is l_0.
Retain figure 223 reference and its figure/caption place; no image authoring.
Length l in K is the distance between endpoint positions recorded at the same time according to synchronized clocks of K; distinguish this measurement from visual appearance.

Equation (8.2): l=l_0 sqrt(1-v^2/c^2). For nonzero subluminal relative speed, its factor is less than 1 and l<l_0; at v=0 the lengths coincide. This is longitudinal contraction, not a claim of transverse contraction.
Relativity of this endpoint distance follows from invariant light speed and relativity of time intervals.
Use the previous lesson's light clock but orient the rod parallel, not perpendicular, to the relative velocity. Keep the longitudinal/transverse orientation distinction.
Pulse leaves A, reflects at B, and returns to A. In K_1 the rod is at rest, each leg is l_0, and (8.3) is c tau_0=2l_0.
Retain figure 224 reference and figure/caption place.
The same emission and reception events have interval tau in K; (8.1) relates tau and tau_0. A single moving A-clock measures proper time, while K uses its own synchronized coordinate clocks.
Define outbound tau_1 and return tau_2, with tau=tau_1+tau_2.
In K, positions AB, A_1B_1, A_2B_2 correspond to 0, tau_1, tau_1+tau_2. The receding mirror advances v tau_1; outbound path is l+v tau_1, so l+v tau_1=c tau_1 and tau_1=l/(c-v).
Retain figure 225 reference and figure/caption place.

On return A approaches the pulse by v tau_2; return path is l-v tau_2, so l-v tau_2=c tau_2 and tau_2=l/(c+v). Raw source reads l= v tau_2 in the preceding sentence; preserve raw source and apply only approved source-bound p0261-math-1 through template errata.
Keep complete (8.4): tau=tau_1+tau_2=2cl/(c^2-v^2)=(2l/c)/(1-v^2/c^2). Keep complete (8.5): tau=tau_0/sqrt(1-v^2/c^2)=(2l_0/c)/sqrt(1-v^2/c^2).
Equate (8.4) and (8.5) for the same event interval to derive (8.2), not merely state an unrelated formula.
Measured longitudinal distance is frame-dependent and depends on relative speed.

For the same rod the proper length is greater than any longitudinal moving-frame length at nonzero speed. Reverse the rest/moving roles of K and K_1: a rod at rest in K has proper length l_0 there and a contracted length in K_1. Reciprocity follows from the relativity principle, not a preferred frame.

The source uses Eddington's common-sense warning and a Gulliver literary comparison to express the puzzling reciprocal character of contraction. Remove the fiction; use a neutral comparison of equal-proper-length rods at rest in different frames, with each frame's own simultaneous endpoint measurements. If naming Eddington, identify him only as the source's historical attribution; do not reattribute new explanatory prose or call the fiction science.
